sections.html:
Gaithersburg is a city in Montgomery County, northwest of Washington, D.C. The 2020 count was 69,657 residents in 25,908 households, which made it the third-largest incorporated city in Maryland.

The boundary has quirks. The NIST campus west of I-270 and several other enclaves inside the city's edges are unincorporated county land. Before you assume a house falls under city rules, confirm whether the address is inside the city limits or only next to them. A house near Metro, MARC or I-270 is also easier to explain to out-of-area buyers.

Montgomery County collects residential property taxes and puts the Gaithersburg portion on the county bill. The combined rate includes a special rate of 20.56 cents. A county-wide special rate of $0.3180 brings a Montgomery County property outside a municipality to $1.0392.

The state reassessed Montgomery County for January 1, 2026, with residential values up 12.6% on average since 2023. Increases phase in over three years.

Applications for the state Homeowners Property Tax Credit filed by May 1 are applied to the tax bill, and those filed by September 1 produce a revised bill or certificate. Call Montgomery County Finance at (240) 777-8860 to confirm bill dates and your payoff when you sell.

Montgomery's transfer tax varies with property value, and a recordation surcharge applies to transactions over $500,000. Your title company will print the exact figures on the settlement statement.

These neighboring planned communities in west Gaithersburg usually come with community rules and fees. Kentlands began in 1988 on a former farm, with a downtown commercial district, lakes, trails and pocket parks, and the first residents moved in during 1991. The Kentlands Citizens Assembly runs shared facilities such as pools, tennis courts and a clubhouse.

If your house is in a planned community, ask the association early for its governing documents, current fees and any open violations. A buyer will want those papers, and gathering them takes time. Request them before you list or accept any offer.

All rental properties, including apartments and single-family homes, need a city rental license that is renewed every two years. Before a final license is issued, staff do a full interior and exterior inspection to confirm the dwelling meets housing codes.

The Neighborhood Services Team enforces the City Code on property maintenance, public nuisances, rental housing and landlord-tenant relations. A revised Chapter 13 on landlord-tenant relations took effect January 1, 2025, covering radon testing, landlord-tenant communication, ratio utility billing and relocation assistance. Before closing on a rental, call 301-258-6340 or email RentalHousing@gaithersburgMD.gov to ask what happens to the license.

Ask the city whether your license is current and whether any inspection items are open. An unresolved code item can slow a retail sale, and a cash buyer will price it in.

Interstate 270 runs northwest from the Capital Beltway to I-70 at Frederick, with Maryland Route 355 (Frederick Avenue) parallel as the main commercial road. The Shady Grove Metro station, the Red Line's northwestern terminus, is just outside the city. MARC stops in the city are Gaithersburg (Old Town) and Metropolitan Grove.

sections.h2: What Maryland requires you to disclose
sections.html: Sellers of homes with one to four units give the buyer a disclosure or disclaimer form. If it arrives late, the buyer has a right to rescind within 5 days. In an estate sale, the personal representative handles the sale and may be exempt from the disclosure rule, so ask the estate's attorney which form applies.

• Association paperwork and fees for a house in a planned community.
  • A rental license and inspection history for a leased house.
  • A tax bill that carries a city portion on the county bill.
  • An estate sale where the family lives elsewhere and no one maintains the house.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so these items matter less to timing. They still have to be settled before the deed is recorded, and the closing agent pays any tax balance or lien from your proceeds.

1. Confirm the address is inside Gaithersburg's limits.
  2. Collect association documents, if any, and the latest tax bill.
  3. Check the rental license and any open inspection items.
  4. Complete the Maryland disclosure or disclaimer form and give it to the buyer with the contract.
  5. Review the settlement statement for the tax proration, then close.

Keep copies of everything you hand over. If a question comes up after closing, a paper trail answers it quickly. If the city or county sends a notice while your house is under contract, forward it to the title company the same day.

sections.h2: What the house-sale timeline looks like
sections.html:
Most of the delay in a sale comes from paperwork, not from the buyer. In Gaithersburg that usually means three requests: the association for its documents, the city for rental license status, and Montgomery County Finance for the tax payoff. Send all three on the same day and the answers tend to arrive together.

With a traditional buyer, the lender's appraisal and underwriting add weeks and can reopen the price. A cash buyer has no lender, so the closing date depends mainly on the title search and your documents. Ask for a closing date in writing, and ask who pays the transfer and recordation costs, since the contract decides that split.

sections.h2: What to have ready before an offer
sections.html:
• The deed or the name on the current tax bill.
  • The latest county tax bill, showing the Gaithersburg portion.
  • Association documents and fee schedule, for Kentlands, Lakelands or any other planned community.
  • The rental license and any inspection report, for a leased house.
  • A list of repairs you know about, since latent defects must be disclosed whether or not you use the disclaimer.

Having these in a folder lets you answer a buyer the same day. Slow answers are the most common reason a fast sale becomes a slow one.

Gaithersburg began as a farming settlement. It was incorporated on April 5, 1878, and became a city in 1968. A 1,000-acre tract along I-270 became part of IBM's headquarters in the late 1960s and 1970s, and rapid suburban growth from the 1970s onward replaced the farming character. Older sections near Old Town carry that history, and their houses often need more repairs than newer subdivisions.

faqs.q: Is Gaithersburg's property tax on the Montgomery County bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Montgomery County collects residential property taxes and includes the Gaithersburg portion on the county bill. The city's residential rate is 26.2 cents per $100 of assessed value.

faqs.q: Does Gaithersburg require a rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. All rental properties, including single-family homes, need a city license renewed every two years, and staff inspect the interior and exterior before the final license is issued.

faqs.q: What is the combined tax rate in Gaithersburg?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 combined rate is $1.1888 per $100 of assessed value. Your own bill depends on your assessed value and credits.

faqs.q: Is the NIST campus inside Gaithersburg?
faqs.a: No. NIST sits west of I-270 on unincorporated county land. Check whether your own address is inside the city before assuming city rules apply.

faqs.q: What should I request from my HOA before selling in Kentlands or Lakelands?
faqs.a: Ask for the governing documents, the current fee schedule and any open violation notices. Start early, because the association's paperwork often takes time.
